newsitem.title: INDIA: OPINION - WEEKLY TECHNICAL ANALYSIS OF BOMBAY SHARE INDEX.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - WEEKLY TECHNICAL ANALYSIS OF BOMBAY SHARE INDEX.

text.p: INDICATORS ON THE MONTHLY CHART SHOW THAT THE RALLY MAY
FIZZLE OUT NEXT FORTNIGHT is a trend analysis of the 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index for the period August 4 to August 8 by analyst Mehmood Khan at Times Guaranty Financials Ltd

Trading for the week ended on a buoyant note, with a gain of 157.51 points (3.76 percent) at 4347.32 levels over the previous week. The majority of the pivotals tracked on the monthly bar chart, depict that the rise has been on declining volume, exhibits that the rally from 4105.28 may lose momentum in the next two weeks.

The technicals of majority of the pivotals have further deteriorated as Price oscillator, Trix & Stochastic have turned bearish on the monthly bar charts. The trend is exhibiting a slow speed of ascent and is close to the triggers that would start the beginning of correction.
The resistance levels for the Sensex are 4405 and 4470. The minor top formation is expected on Tuesday, Wednesday in the range 4405-4470 with a stop loss of 4488.

The minor rally from 4105.28, has retraced the decline of a smaller degree by 73.23 percent (4356.55). The cycle theory shows that the change in trend (CIT), is due and may occur on 5th/6th August 1997. The mechanical oscillators in conjunction with the volume justify that the minor top may be formed at 4415-4470 levels.

As per the time cycle theory, the Sensex may move into the CIT time window on Monday/Wednesday. Hopefully, an upday is formed on Monday. An upday is said to be formed when the Sensex makes a higher high and a higher low with respect to the previous day range of movement.

An upday formation on Monday/Wednesday would result in a clear three days trend running into the time zone. And if this were to happen then a minor top formation cannot be ruled out. The present CIT date enjoys 11 clusters which is reasonably high. Anything above eight clusters is considered high.

The trend in Apollo Tyres, Bajaj Auto, BHEL, Bombay Dyeing, Cadbury, Castrol, Colgate, Dr. Reddy Labs, Escorts, Glaxo, Hindustan Lever, Hindalco, HPCL, ICICI, IFCI, ITC, L&T, Reliance, Tata Chemicals, Tisco, Tata Tea are indicating losing momentum.

These counters may seek higher values in the initial half of the week, but may witness selling pressure in due course and may probably close the week on a weak note. If the base support does not widen, then the current rally may not continue. The best trading opportunity for the week is to be on the short side from Tuesday with a strict stop-loss of 4488 levels.

The price following oscillators on the weekly bar chart are exhibiting that the top may be formed at 4405-4435 levels - Relative Strength Index (14 RSI) is 68.99, Price Rate of Change (12 ROC) is placed at 15.34, short term stochastic is hovering at 41.60 and its trigger line is at 53.27, while the medium term stochastic is 78.59 and the trigger is 81.36, the Macd is 193.08 and its trigger is 162.87, the price oscillator is 0.93, 14 William's percent R is placed at -12.69 and Trix is 1.08.
The Price oscillator, Trix and William's R percent are indicating negative divergence.

For the current week, the BSE Sensex in the upmove may encounter resistance at 4385, 4115 and 4458 levels and on the lower end it may find support at 4271-4226 level. The National Index may witness profit booking at 1934-1961 level and support at 1863 level.
